supporting_observations.claim: At 13:37–13:39 UTC, WS-MLOPEZ-01 obtained Kerberos tickets for FILE-HD-01 and DC-HD-01 using its machine account; the records do not identify a user initiating this activity.

At 13:57 UTC, FILE-HD-01 resolved WS-MLOPEZ-01 and initiated a TCP connection to its RPC endpoint mapper on port 135. The connection record has state S2 and does not establish successful remote execution.

At 13:44 UTC, WS-MLOPEZ-01 used the proxy to download about 38.8 MB from download.windowsupdate.com with a Windows Update Agent user agent. This is consistent with patching, but does not establish who initiated it or whether it was authorized.

At 14:11 UTC, GoogleDriveFS.exe launched from Explorer under maria.lopez's account, and a loaded module was reported as validly signed by Google. Google Drive is not among the approved services in the supplied environment context; these records do not show that data was uploaded.

The provided process records around 14:11–14:17 show svchost.exe accessing LSASS, a short-lived SYSTEM conhost.exe process, and WmiPrvSE.exe processes. They do not identify PowerShell or provide a PowerShell command line, and they occur after the reported 13:40 window.

known_telemetry_limitations: The submitted records do not include a PowerShell process-creation event, script-block or transcription logs, or a process tree explaining the reported window.
The provided evidence does not include process or command records from WS-OHADDAD-01 or FILE-HD-01 that would identify who initiated the port-135 connection or what it did.
The records do not include RPC/WMI operational details, file-share auditing for the relevant activity, or evidence tying the observed Kerberos tickets to a particular script or action.
The supplied proxy records show Windows Update traffic and GoogleDriveFS startup, but do not establish patch authorization or Google Drive data transfer.
claims_not_established: That PowerShell actually ran on WS-MLOPEZ-01 at about 13:40 UTC, or what command or script it may have executed.
That the FILE-HD-01 connection resulted in successful remote administration or was related to the reported PowerShell window.
That the Windows Update download was initiated by authorized IT patching.
That Google Drive was used to upload or exfiltrate organizational data.
That the observed activity was malicious or, alternatively, that it was all benign.
additional_evidence_needed: Collect complete endpoint process-creation and parent-child telemetry for WS-MLOPEZ-01 from 13:20–14:20 UTC, including PowerShell, console-host, and WMI-related events.
Retrieve PowerShell operational, script-block, and transcription logs for WS-MLOPEZ-01 covering the review window.
Review FILE-HD-01 and WS-OHADDAD-01 process, authentication, SMB-share, and remote-management logs around 13:37–14:18 UTC; correlate them with the TCP 135 connection.
Verify patch deployment records, the identity of the initiator, and whether the Windows Update activity corresponds to the scheduled workstation patching.
Check GoogleDriveFS configuration and sync or proxy telemetry to determine whether it transferred files or was merely launched.
